input: Review contract cuad2-ritterpharmaceuticalsinc and route it.
notes: Customer = Sekisui Diagnostics ('Sekisui'), the exclusive distributor that buys the Products from Qualigen (c13 s.4.7) and funds Qualigen's Development Plan with up to $6,200,000 of Financing Payments (c13 s.4.5); supplier = Qualigen. Distribution and development agreement, so Sekisui is a reseller, not pure buyer paper. Governing law: Delaware (c51). There is no limitation-of-liability clause at all (c31 only excludes consequential damages from the third-party 'Losses' the indemnities cover; c27 adds liquidated damages against Qualigen), so LIAB-CAP is out of scope and the missing cap is tested by route=escalate, as in cuad-americasshoppingmall. CUAD's Ip Ownership Assignment span is the Abandoned Joint IP sentence in c23, which favours Sekisui; it does not decide IP-OWN, which turns on c23 s.8.2 and c55 s.15.16 (label is ours). CUAD Exclusivity spans in c5 were checked: the purchase-exclusivity sentence binds Sekisui. NONCOMPETE is a literal reading: the exclusivity covers only Qualigen's own Products, so it is narrow in practice, but it binds the customer for the five-year auto-renewing term, past the 12-month fallback. Exhibits A-F (pricing formulae, development plan, process flows) do not change any label. DATA-PROT left out: no personal-data terms.

checks.why: c5: extended 'for an additional one (1) year period unless either Party notifies the other Party not less than six (6) months before the end': notice window over 60 days.
c15 s.4.10: payments more than 30 days past due 'shall accrue interest ... at an annual rate equal to the prime rate ... plus an additional 200 basis points (2%)'.

c23: 'Qualigen shall own all right, title and interest' in the Development IP that Sekisui's Financing Payments fund, and c55: 'No right or license is granted to Sekisui by implication ... to any know-how, patent or other intellectual property right owned or controlled by Qualigen': no perpetual licence back.

c5: 'Sekisui shall purchase the Products exclusively from Qualigen' for a worldwide Territory over a five-year auto-renewing term, and c7 bars Sekisui from selling to the Qualigen Retained Customers: exclusivity binding the customer beyond the 12-month fallback.
c49 s.15.2: not assignable 'without the written consent of the other', except either party to a successor on a merger or sale of the business: the playbook fallback.
c41 s.13.1: obligations apply 'during the Term and for a period of five (5) years following the expiration or termination': within 3-5 years.

c31: indemnities are mutual and only for 'claims, suits and proceedings by a Third Party': Sekisui for its negligence and breaches (s.11.1), Qualigen for product injury, negligence, breaches and IP infringement (s.11.2, c33).
English-only contract; no bilingual text.

c13 s.4.7: 'Sekisui shall pay for each Product ... within 30 days after Sekisui has received the applicable invoice'; true-ups are due 30 days from invoice (c11) and Financing Payments fall due only on achievement of milestones (c13 s.4.5), so nothing is prepaid.
c47 s.14.3: 'Sekisui may terminate this Agreement ... at any other time upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice'; a customer-only convenience right with no fee, so the hint is not met.
No limitation-of-liability clause anywhere, so nothing caps Sekisui's liability (c31 only excludes consequential damages from indemnified Losses).

input: Review contract cuad2-webhelpcominc and route it.
notes: Customer = Eliance Corporation ('Customer'), which pays eGain for hosted access to eGain's software; supplier = eGain. Exhibit A (fees, Additional Fees) is referenced but not included. CUAD's Cap On Liability spans are eGain's sole-remedy clauses (c10, c17, c19) and its c22 cap, all of which limit only eGain; CUAD's Uncapped Liability span is c22's consequential-damages exclusion with the IP carve-out, also about eGain. Nothing caps Customer's liability, hence the LIAB-CAP finding. Governing law: California (c32). IP-OWN left out: Online Messages are Customer's property (c7), but eGain owns 'any and all modifications as a result of any implementation services', which would be bought under a Statement of Work that is not included, so whether there are bespoke deliverables is undecidable. DATA-PROT left out: eGain disclaims any guarantee of privacy or security (c21) and keeps copies of Online Messages after termination (c30), but there are no location, transfer or breach-notice terms for the hint to bite on cleanly.

checks.why: c22 limits only 'eGain's entire liability' (to the price paid for the Services out of which the claim arose) and c18 makes the credits eGain's sole liability; nothing caps Customer's liability: one-sided cap.

c8: 'CUSTOMER AGREES TO PAY FOR HOSTING SERVICES ON OR BEFORE THE FIRST DAY OF THE MONTH IN WHICH THE HOSTING SERVICES ARE PROVIDED': 100% in advance; c30 also makes accrued fees due 'Within fifteen (15) days' of termination.
c8: late payment 'shall be subject to a late fee equal to one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month': recurring monthly percentage.
c23 sets no duration and c30 makes Section 8 survive 'any expiration or termination' with no time limit and no trade-secret limit: perpetual.
c33: 'Neither party may assign ... without the prior written consent of the other party', except either party on a merger or sale of all or substantially all of its business: the playbook fallback.
c26: renews 'for successive one (1) year periods unless either party gives ... at least thirty (30) days prior written notice': within the required position.
The only indemnity is eGain's defence of third-party IP infringement suits against Customer (c24); Customer gives none.
English-only contract; no bilingual text.
No exclusivity or non-compete binds Customer; c31 only lets eGain list Customer as a reference.
One-year term renewing yearly (c26); neither party has a convenience right (c26/c29 termination is for breach or insolvency) and the term is not over 12 months.
Critical LIAB-CAP finding: c22 caps only eGain's liability, Customer's is uncapped.

input: Review contract cuad2-integrityfunds and route it.
notes: Customer = the Integrity Short Term Government Fund ('Fund'), which receives underwriting/distribution services and pays Integrity the Rule 12b-1 distribution and service fees (c3 s.1.7, c5 s.2.3); supplier = Integrity Funds Distributor ('Integrity'). Fund-industry underwriting agreement, not ordinary buyer paper. Governing law: Kansas (c15). There is no limitation-of-liability clause at all (c13 s.8.2 only makes the Fund's obligations non-recourse to its trustees and shareholders; it sets no amount), so LIAB-CAP is out of scope and the missing cap is tested by route=escalate, as in cuad-americasshoppingmall. CUAD has no Termination For Convenience annotation, but c13 gives the Fund a 60-day no-penalty right; the TERM-CONV label is ours (CUAD omission overruled). Left out: PAY-TERMS (fees are 'payable in the manner and terms set forth in the Plan', which is not included), CONF-TERM (the agreement has no confidentiality clause at all, so there is no term to judge), DATA-PROT (no data terms).

checks.why: c13: 'This Agreement will also terminate automatically in the event of its assignment (as defined in the 1940 Act)': Integrity cannot assign it to anyone.

c13: after 18 January 2022 it continues 'for successive annual periods' only 'provided such continuance is specifically approved at least annually' by the Fund's Board: one-year renewals that need the Fund's approval.

Indemnities are reciprocal and tied to actions brought against the indemnified party: the Fund covers misstatements in its registration statement (c7), Integrity covers unauthorised sales literature and information it furnished (c9).
No late-payment interest or charge anywhere.
No IP or data ownership terms; nothing gives Integrity the Fund's data or any bespoke deliverable.
English-only contract; no bilingual text.
Nothing restricts the Fund; c13 s.8.1 even lets Integrity distribute for other investment companies.

c13: 'terminable with respect to the Fund, without penalty, (a) on 60 days' written notice' by vote of the Qualified Trustees or the shareholders: meets the required position (Integrity's own right needs 90 days).
No limitation-of-liability clause anywhere, so nothing caps the Fund's liability (c13 s.8.2 is only a no-personal-liability clause).

input: Review contract cuad2-wppplc and route it.
notes: Customer = WPP 2005 Limited ('Company'), which receives and pays for John Rogers' ('Executive', the supplier) services as CFO; this is an executive service (employment) agreement, so several rules fit badly. Out of scope: LIAB-CAP (no limitation clause anywhere, so no clause to cite; the missing cap is tested by route=escalate, as in cuad-americasshoppingmall); PAY-TERMS (salary paid monthly in arrears through payroll, c29, no invoices, so the rule does not map); CONF-TERM (clause 13, c40/c42, binds only the Executive with no time limit: 'perpetual' on the literal rule but it runs in the customer's favour, so a grader should not punish either answer); INDEMNITY (the only indemnity is c35 9.7, the Executive's benefit of the indemnity in the Company's articles, whose terms are not in the text); ASSIGN (no assignment clause, CUAD Anti-Assignment = No; the Executive's service is personal (c27) and c49 15.12 contemplates the Company transferring its business, so 'silent' does not cleanly mean 'supplier may assign freely'); DATA-PROT (c54 19.1 covers only the Executive's own data); GOV-LAW (English law and exclusive English courts, c57).

checks.why: c46: 15.1 'terminated by either party giving the other at least 12 months' notice' on an open-ended term; 15.2 lets the Company end it at once only with a Payment in Lieu equal to the full notice period's salary and benefits: notice over 90 days, or a penalty.
No renewal mechanism: the Appointment runs indefinitely until notice under c46 (CUAD Renewal Term blank, Expiration 'perpetual').
No late-payment interest or charge anywhere.
c44 14.2: IP created by the Executive 'shall belong to and vest in the Company', and 14.3 assigns anything that does not vest by law: the customer owns the deliverables.
English-only contract; no bilingual text.

The restrictions in c38 ('the Executive may not accept any employment') and Schedule 3 (c91) bind only the Executive, the supplier; nothing restricts the Company. CUAD's Non-Compete = Yes points at those supplier covenants.
No clause caps the Company's liability at all (CUAD Cap On Liability = No); c35 only excludes its liability for pension tax charges and insurer refusals. Governing law is present (c57, English law).

input: Review contract cuad2-inktomicorp and route it.
notes: Customer = Microsoft, which receives the hosting and maintenance services and pays Inktomi's monthly fees (c3, c32); supplier = Inktomi. Heavily redacted ('[*]'), and one of a package of Ancillary Agreements (c4) that are not included. Route: escalate because the cap in c54 cannot be read; if the redacted text were a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees, the route would be negotiate (TERM-CONV, PAY-TERMS and GOV-LAW are major). Out of scope: LIAB-CAP (c54 is mutual 'NEITHER PARTY' but its amount, kind of damages and carve-out are redacted; CUAD marks the same span as both Cap On Liability and Uncapped Liability); IP-OWN (ownership of the Product, the bespoke deliverable, is left to the Software Development Agreement, c44, not included; Usage Data is jointly owned with Microsoft's share redacted, c19; Inktomi owns Web Indexing Data, c18); CONF-TERM (governed by a separate 1997 NDA, c45, not included); DATA-PROT; GOV-LAW (Washington law, c74).

checks.why: c55 10.2: Microsoft may terminate 'without cause upon [*] ([*]) days prior written notice', but Inktomi may then elect 'an early termination penalty' (c56-c57: Microsoft pays [*] of the outstanding loan amounts): a convenience right only with a penalty, on an indefinite term; Inktomi's own right (one year's notice, c55) is not the <= 90-day mutual fallback.

c34: the 4.1(b) new-server fee is due 'Notwithstanding section 4.2 below ... in immediately available funds on the first business day of each month', with no invoice: due sooner than 30 days after receipt (other fees are net [*] days from receipt, c38, redacted).

c76: 'neither party may transfer, assign or sublicense this Agreement ... except with the express written consent of the other party', with mergers and changes of control counted as transfers; Exhibit F (c106-c111) lets Inktomi transfer on a merger only after building Microsoft a separate cluster and licensing the Product, and the Agreement then terminates: not free assignment.
No renewal: c11 'Term' continues 'indefinitely until this Agreement is terminated pursuant to Section 10' (CUAD Renewal Term blank, Expiration 'perpetual').

c51 8.1: 'Each party shall ... defend [*] party claim or action brought against the Indemnified Party': mutual and for claims brought by others; the tax indemnities in c41 are also reciprocal (Inktomi Taxes / Microsoft Taxes).
No late-payment interest; 'interest' appears only for the Loan Agreement and tax penalties (c41, c56).
English-only contract; no bilingual text.
CUAD Non-Compete and Exclusivity = No, verified: c24 lets Microsoft host the Product elsewhere at any time and c26 leaves Inktomi free to serve others; c46 restricts only Inktomi.

c54 'LIMITATION OF LIABILITY' is redacted to 'NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE [*] ... FOR ANY [*], [*] OR [*] [*]' with an 'EXCEPT FOR [*]' carve-out: no visible wording caps Microsoft's liability or shows a cap of at least 12 months' fees, so a lawyer must decide.

input: Review contract cuad2-slovakwirelessfinancecobv and route it.
notes: Customer = EuroTel Bratislava a.s., which receives and pays for Sicap's maintenance and support (c12, c46); supplier = Sicap Ltd. There is no governing-law or forum clause anywhere (CUAD Governing Law blank), which on its own also escalates. AUTO-RENEW: the 6-week window misses the required 30 days but is inside the 60-day fallback, so no finding (fallback = compliant, as in the first suite). c45 makes the General Terms and Conditions of the original Swisscom Purchase and License Contract (not included) 'also valid for Maintenance and Support'. Out of scope: CONF-TERM (no confidentiality clause in this document; it may sit in those incorporated terms); DATA-PROT (silent while Sicap gets remote access and memory dumps of the prepaid system, c22-c23; the hint does not cleanly decide it); GOV-LAW (absent).

checks.why: c56: 'Sicap Ltd's liability for indirect loss ... is excluded' and c49 excuses Sicap for suspension damages; nothing limits EuroTel's liability: a one-sided limitation that leaves us uncapped. (CUAD's Cap On Liability = Yes is this supplier-only exclusion, not a cap on us.)
c46: 'Maintenance and Support fees are payable semi-annually in advance': 100% prepayment of each period; c48 also runs the 30 days from 'the invoice date', not receipt.

Two-year initial term (c53) and CUAD Termination For Convenience = No, verified: EuroTel may end it only for uncured substantial breach (c55), at a renewal date (c54), or within one month of a supplier price-increase offer (c53): no convenience right on a term over 12 months.
c57: rights and obligations 'may not be assigned ... by either party without the prior written consent', except to a majority-owned subsidiary by written notice: the playbook fallback.
c54: renews 'for a period of one year' unless terminated 'at least six (6) weeks prior to the renewal date': 12-month renewals and a 42-day window, inside the 60-day fallback.
No indemnity anywhere in the contract; we give none.
No late-payment interest or charge; the only remedy for late payment is suspension after notice (c49).
Support-only contract for Sicap's own software with no ownership terms (CUAD Ip Ownership Assignment = No); no customer data or bespoke deliverables go to Sicap.
English-only contract; no bilingual text.
CUAD Non-Compete and Exclusivity = No, verified: nothing restricts EuroTel.
Critical LIAB-CAP finding: c56 limits only Sicap's liability; there is also no governing-law clause at all.

input: Review contract cuad2-pareteumcorp and route it.
notes: Customer = Elephant Talk ('ELEPHANT TALK'), which 'shall purchase the Hosting Services from T-Mobile' and pays for them (c26, c60-c64); supplier = T-Mobile Netherlands. Heavy '***' redactions: the Initial Term length (c94), the renewal period (c95), the payment period in 9.2.4 (c65), the cap amounts (c80) and T-Mobile/Elephant Talk termination rights 18.1(d)-(f) (c99). Labels rest only on visible words: 2.3 (c28) calls the article 17.2 notice 'the twelve month termination notice', which fixes the non-renewal window and shows the Initial Term exceeds 12 months. CUAD overruled twice: Termination For Convenience = Yes points at the c95 end-of-term notice, which is non-renewal, not convenience termination; Non-Compete/Exclusivity = No misses the c28 bar on Elephant Talk sourcing similar Hosting Services elsewhere. CUAD Cap On Liability/Uncapped Liability (c80, c82) are accurate; the LIAB-CAP finding rests on who the c82 carve-outs actually uncap. DATA-PROT left out: c55-c57 give purpose limitation and Dutch DPA compliance but say nothing on location, transfers or breach notice, so the hint does not cleanly decide it. GOV-LAW out of scope (c109: laws of the Netherlands, courts of The Hague).

checks.why: c82 lifts the c80 cap for gross negligence and for 'article 15 (indemnification for breach of intellectual property rights)', and the only article 15 indemnity is Elephant Talk's to T-Mobile (c91 15.4), while c80 applies 'Without prejudice to the provisions expressly stated elsewhere' (our indemnities in c68, c94): our IP indemnity is uncapped and unreciprocated, beyond the fallback carve-outs; cap amounts are redacted.

Elephant Talk 'shall indemnify T-Mobile against high usage, fraud and bed debts/non-payment of its ELEPHANT TALK Customers' (c68) and 'for all damages and losses T-Mobile suffers' from customers' device misuse (c94): first-party indemnities, plus third-party (c82 12.6) and IP (c91 15.4) indemnities; T-Mobile gives none.

Elephant Talk can exit only by 'the twelve month termination notice' before the end of an Initial Term over 12 months (c28, c95) or for breach/insolvency (c97, c99): no convenience right. Overrules CUAD's Termination For Convenience = Yes, whose c95 span is end-of-term non-renewal.

c95: 'the Agreement will be automatically extended for consecutive *** periods until such time as *** termination notice is provided', and c28 calls that notice 'the twelve month termination notice': notice window over 60 days.

c62: the second installment of the upfront development contribution (c60) 'shall be paid by ELEPHANT TALK within fifteen (15) Calendar Days of the invoice date', charged on signing before any service: due in fewer than 30 days.
c67: late invoices 'shall bear interest ("enkelvoudig") on a daily basis at the rate of the legal commercial interest rate ("wettelijke handelsrente") plus 1 %'.

c28: 'ELEPHANT TALK will not enter into any discussions or agreement on the provisioning of (similar) Hosting Services ... with any *** in the Netherlands for the duration of the Initial Term' (over 12 months), and c29-c30 restrict whom it may serve. Overrules CUAD's Non-Compete/Exclusivity = No.
c79: 'This article 11 shall survive the termination of this Agreement ... for a period of two (2) years': shorter than 3 years.

c103-c104: 'neither Party shall sell, transfer or assign this Agreement' except in whole to an Affiliated Company that assumes all obligations and whose financial strength the other Party approves in writing in advance: T-Mobile cannot assign freely.

Customer data stays ours: 'All rights to the personal and traffic data related to ELEPHANT TALK Customers ... shall rest in ELEPHANT TALK' (c55); T-Mobile keeps only its own Hosting Services IP and licenses it to us (c91 15.5-15.6); no bespoke deliverables pass to T-Mobile.
c112: 'The Agreement is written in the English language'; Dutch legal terms in parentheses are glosses, not a second text.
Critical LIAB-CAP finding: c82 leaves Elephant Talk's IP indemnity (c91) uncapped while T-Mobile gives none, and the c80 cap amounts are redacted.

input: Review contract cuad2-reynoldsconsumerproductsinc and route it.
notes: Two-way transition services agreement. Customer = Reynolds Consumer Products ('Company'/'RCP'), Recipient and payer of the Exhibit A Transition Services (IT hosting, HR, finance, tax, legal; c72-c113); supplier = RGHI. RCP also provides small, mostly free Reverse Transition Services to RGHI (Exhibit B, c113-c118); labels judge the contract from RCP's side as buyer. Unsigned S-1 exhibit with a blank date. CUAD Cap On Liability (c52, c53) is accurate; CUAD Uncapped Liability = No is partly overruled: the c53 cap reaches only liability 'in relation to services provided', so RCP's c66 guarantee indemnity is not capped. CUAD Termination For Convenience = Yes (c35) is accurate as far as it goes, but the same clause and the Exhibit A terms lock the 24-month G1 IT services to an agreed Migration Plan. DATA-PROT left out: c22 gives prompt Security Incident notice but no time limit or location terms, and data sits in RGHI or cloud data centres (c72); the hint does not cleanly decide it. GOV-LAW out of scope (c61: Illinois law, exclusive Lake County courts).

checks.why: c53: 'IN NO EVENT SHALL A PARTY'S LIABILITY IN RELATION TO SERVICES PROVIDED UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE FEES PAID TO IT UNDER THIS AGREEMENT FOR THE SPECIFIC SERVICE THAT RESULTED IN THE LOSS': a per-service cap, not 12 months of fees, and it covers only service liability, so RCP's c66 indemnity for 'any and all losses' under the RGHI Guarantees is uncapped.

c66: 'RCP shall indemnify RGHI and its Affiliates against any and all losses suffered or incurred in connection with the Company under the RGHI Guarantees or RGHI Letters of Credit': a one-way first-party indemnity RGHI does not reciprocate; the mutual c49 indemnity also covers first-party 'Losses' from material breach, not only third-party claims.

c35 allows 30 days' convenience notice, but the G1 IT services 'may not be terminated independently except in accordance with an agreed Migration Plan' on a '24 months from the Commencement Date' term (c72, c75; Migration Services 'cannot be terminated', c84), and 'any unamortized costs ... will be passed through to the Terminating Party'.

c29: invoices issued 'within 15 days after the end of each month' are payable 'no later than the last business day of the month Recipient received such invoice': usually fewer than 30 days after receipt.
c29: late amounts 'shall bear interest at the Applicable Rate', defined in c4 as the prime rate 'plus two percent (2%)' per annum.
c39: 'Article VII' (incl. 7.4 Confidential Information, c45) survives termination with no time limit and no trade-secret limit: perpetual.

c64: 'No Party may assign this Agreement ... without the prior written consent of the other Party', except to Affiliates, a purchaser of the business or assets, or financing sources for collateral: affiliates/successors, as in the fallback.
c34: each Service runs 'until 12 months following the Commencement Date' or the Exhibit term, then ends; no renewal (CUAD Renewal Term blank).

Each party's IP and 'data ... shall remain the property of such Party' (c21, c48); RGHI must migrate and hand over RCP's systems, data and records (c10, c47, c84). Nothing gives RGHI RCP's data or bespoke deliverables.
English-only contract; no bilingual text.
No exclusivity or non-compete binds RCP; the only restriction is on RGHI ceasing use of the RCP Names (c49).
Critical LIAB-CAP finding: the c53 cap is per-service fees, below 12 months of fees, and leaves RCP's c66 guarantee indemnity uncapped.

input: Review contract cuad2-verticalnetinc and route it.
notes: Customer = Converge, which 'desires to obtain' maintenance and support and pays a $4.5M minimum fee (c2, c46); supplier = VerticalNet and VerticalNet Enterprises ('Vert'/'VNE'). Unsigned execution copy. The companion Subscription License Agreement is referenced but not included; it sets Converge's licence to Enhancements (c41) and remedies for product claims (c56), so the IP-OWN finding rests on what this document says: Vert owns Converge-requested work and takes a perpetual licence to Converge's own materials, with no licence back stated here. CUAD Cap On Liability (6.3 three-month cap, c57-c58), Termination For Convenience = No and Renewal Term (mutual renewal only, c67) verified against the text; no CUAD annotation overruled. DATA-PROT left out: Vert gets remote access to Converge's servers (c24) but the contract has no data-protection terms either way. GOV-LAW out of scope (c79: Pennsylvania law).

checks.why: c57-c58: each party's maximum liability for maintenance and support 'SHALL NOT EXCEED ... THE AMOUNTS PAID BY CONVERGE TO VERT FOR SUCH MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT SERVICES DURING THE THREE MONTH PERIOD IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING' the claim: far below 12 months of fees.

Initial Term from 1 October 2001 'until March 31, 2003' (c67), 18 months, and Converge may terminate only on an Event of Default (c68, c69); the 18 Monthly Installments are 'non-refundable' (c46): no convenience right on a term over 12 months.

c46: the first installment is due 'on the date this Agreement is executed' and each later one 'no later than the first day of each month', non-refundable: fees paid monthly in advance, not 30 days after an invoice.
c49: overdue amounts 'shall be subject to late charges of the lesser of (a) 1.5% per month of the overdue amount'.

c39: 'Vert shall be the sole and exclusive owner of all Converge-Requested Enhancements', bespoke work Converge pays for, and Converge grants Vert an 'irrevocable, perpetual, world-wide' licence to its own independent materials 'for any and all purposes'; c41 gives Converge no source code and only whatever licence the absent Subscription License Agreement sets.
c73: Section 7 (Confidential Information) survives 'any expiration or termination' with no time limit and no trade-secret limit: perpetual.

c81: 'A party may assign this Agreement to any Affiliate. Otherwise, neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent': affiliate-only carve-out, within the fallback.
c67: 'this Agreement shall renew only upon the mutual written agreement of the parties' for one-year terms: no auto-renewal.
No indemnity in the document; Converge gives none.
English-only contract; no bilingual text.
c82: 'this Agreement is not exclusive as to either party'; the c66 non-solicitation of employees is mutual and not a non-compete.
Critical LIAB-CAP finding: the c57-c58 cap is three months of support fees, far below 12 months.

input: Review contract cuad2-vertexenergyinc and route it.
notes: Customer = Magellan Terminals Holdings ('Owner'), which retains Omega ('Operator') to operate and maintain its Rail Facility (c4, c18); Operator bears its own operating costs (c31, c37) and Owner reimburses only out-of-budget work it orders (c38). CUAD says Cap On Liability = Yes, but its span is the c74 (s.8.8) exclusion of special/indirect/consequential damages, which sets no amount: overruled, and LIAB-CAP is a finding at c74. CONF-TERM left out: the contract has no confidentiality clause at all, so there is no clause to cite. DATA-PROT left out as in the first suite (no personal-data terms; the rule is not cleanly triggered). GOV-LAW (Delaware, c72) out of scope as usual but makes the route at least negotiate.

checks.why: c33: 'Owner hereby releases and shall indemnify, defend and hold Operator harmless from and against any Claim or Loss' from following Owner's instructions, c32 the same for rejected recommendations and c26 for 'any liability accruing ... after the effective date of termination'; Operator gives none of these back, and c62-c63 also cover first-party Claims for 'any breach of this Agreement by Owner'.

c74 (8.8 'Limitation of Liability') only excludes 'special, indirect, consequential, punitive, or exemplary damages'; no amount caps Owner's direct damages or its indemnities (c62, c32, c33): our liability is uncapped.
c78: 'Operator shall not make any assignment ... unless there first shall have been obtained the written consent thereto of Owner'; attempted assignment in violation is 'null and void'.
c21: the Agreement 'shall continue for the duration of the Lease'; no renewal term or non-renewal notice (CUAD Renewal Term empty).
No late-payment interest or charge is imposed; c21 only lists 'any interest' among amounts whose non-payment is a default.

No ownership terms favour Operator; c25 requires it to deliver 'all books and records and other property (including, without limitation, intellectual property) of Owner' on termination, and the improvements are to Owner's own facility.
English-only contract; no bilingual text.
No exclusivity or non-compete (CUAD Non-Compete and Exclusivity = No); c65 expressly keeps Owner free to build and operate other rail facilities.
Owner pays no service fee; the only payments are reimbursements of out-of-scope work it orders (c38) with no short due date and no prepayment.
c24: Owner may terminate '(e) Without cause on no less than seven (7) days prior written notice'; reimbursing unamortized capex is optional ('Owner may reimburse'), so no penalty.
Critical LIAB-CAP finding: c74 excludes consequential damages but nothing caps Owner's liability.

input: Review contract cuad2-etonpharmaceuticalsinc and route it.
notes: Customer = Eton ('ETON'), the exclusive licensee that pays Aucta licence fees, milestones and royalties (c1, c13, c15); supplier = Aucta, which develops and registers the Products at its own cost (c9). CUAD says Cap On Liability = Yes (Uncapped Liability = No), but its span is c37 s.14.1, a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages with no amount: overruled, LIAB-CAP is a finding. CUAD's Non-Compete and Exclusivity spans bind Aucta (c11 s.3.5) or grant ETON an exclusive licence (c9 s.2.1), so they are not NONCOMPETE findings; s.3.5 ends in a redaction and s.5.4 (sales FTEs) is redacted, but no visible text restricts ETON. IP-OWN left out: Aucta keeps ownership of the Products, Dossiers and its Background IP and licenses them exclusively to ETON (c9), but the licence reverts on termination (c27); whether the Dossiers are bespoke deliverables or Aucta's own product IP needs a labelling decision. DATA-PROT left out (pharmacovigilance terms are in Exhibit B, not included). GOV-LAW (Delaware, c37) out of scope.

checks.why: c37 (14.1) only says 'NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES'; no amount caps ETON's direct liability or its c35 indemnity: our liability is uncapped.
c13 (6.1(a)): ETON pays '$2,000,000 within five (5) days of the Effective Date' as an upfront licence fee, which Aucta keeps on termination (c27): payment due in fewer than 30 days.

c27: ETON may end the open-ended term only 'after approval of the Dossier ... upon providing one hundred eighty (180) days' written notice' (before approval only if not approved by 31 Dec 2020): notice over 90 days and no right before approval, on a term over 12 months.

c41: 'The Parties shall not assign ... without the prior written consent of the other Party', except either party on a sale of substantially all its business, merger or change of control with written assumption.
c25: the Term runs until a party terminates under Section 11; no renewal periods or non-renewal notice (CUAD Renewal Term empty, Expiration Date 'Perpetual').
c21: 'This Section 9.1 shall survive termination or expiration of this Agreement and continue in effect thereafter for a period of five (5) years'.
c33 and c35: mutual indemnities, each only for 'Third Party Claims made or suits brought against' the other party (breach, product handling/marketing, negligence).
No late-payment interest or charge; 'interest' appears only in the c5 definition of Losses.
English-only contract; c37 says only that any convenience translation is not official and the English version prevails, and no bilingual text exists.

The only restrictions bind the supplier: c11 (3.5) 'Aucta shall not research, develop, manufacture ... more than two products containing ... Lamotrigine', and c9 grants ETON an exclusive licence; nothing restricts ETON.
Critical LIAB-CAP finding: c37 excludes consequential damages but nothing caps ETON's liability.
